notes: IAM-2 workflows live in the Ticketing.IAM domain as resources + actions; do not model as ad-hoc controllers.
Use Ash policies to authorize only org-scoped admin actors to create/revoke invites.
accept_invite_intent MUST be callable by an anonymous actor given a valid proof token (policy based on token scope).
Persist only token_hash; raw token exists only in memory and outbound email composition.
Use changes to set expires_at and validations for purpose scope.
Consume action MUST be idempotent and MUST use DB uniqueness + transactions to prevent duplicate membership grants.
Workers MUST re-check invite/token status and actor liveness/permission at execution time (GC-032 pattern).
If revoked/expired, worker MUST abort without delivering secrets and MUST emit an audit event.

side_effects_and_jobs.rule: No direct email or external calls inside core actions; enqueue OBQC-controlled jobs with deterministic payloads.

changes: Invalid/expired proof tokens now map to ERR_NOT_FOUND to prevent existence leaks at the boundary.
Standardized required error codes to ERR-1 top-level registry (removed non-registry codes).
Strengthened uniform response rules: hide-existence + stable envelope + timing hardening mandated for all IAM-2 boundary flows.
change_log.summary: Align IAM-2 enumeration hardening with TEN-1@1.7.11 + SEC-1@3.0.11 uniform tenant-safe boundary responses (GC-030/GC-032 posture).

changes: Initial IAM-2 contract introducing tenant-safe silent-link invite workflows (GC-030) and proof token semantics.
Defines proof token hashing, TTL bounds, and idempotent consumption rules.
Requires async workers to re-check authorization and status at execution time (GC-032 pattern).

changelog.summary: Expand IAM-2 into the Gate: add Consumer OTP lane + Consumer Proof Grants; update boundaries; add OTP resources/workflows/security controls; align with tiered security model (consumer vs admin).

constraints: All resources that include org_id MUST enforce org_id presence at the DB level and via Ash validations.
No workflow MUST store raw email/phone identifiers inside invite/token resources; only hashes (raw identifier MAY exist only in outbound email content generation inputs).
Consumer OTP challenges MUST store only destination_hash + code_hash (no plaintext phone/email or code). Plaintext destinations belong in PII-1 only.
consumer_otp_challenge MUST be single-use: on successful verification it MUST transition to status=consumed and set consumed_at_utc; further verifies MUST return uniform responses.
OTP verification MUST enforce max_attempts (recommended 5). Exceeding max_attempts MUST set locked_until_utc (recommended 5m) and status=locked.
consumer_proof_grant MUST be bound to (actor_id, session_id) and MUST NOT be interpreted as strong assurance (aal2_strong) or as IAM-3 StepUpGrant.

resources.name: invite_intent
notes: target_identifier_hash MUST be a one-way normalized hash of the identifier (e.g., lowercased email) using a platform pepper.
Creating a new pending invite for the same (org_id,target_identifier_hash) MUST revoke any prior pending invite (deterministic latest-wins).

resources.name: proof_token
notes: token_hash MUST be computed over the raw token plus a server-side pepper and MUST be compared in constant time.
A consumed token MUST NOT be reusable; replays MUST return a uniform invalid/expired response.

resources.name: invite_claim
notes: invite_claim enables a subject to accept an invite without revealing whether a user account already exists.
Consuming a claim MUST be idempotent: repeated consumption yields the same result without duplicating memberships.

resources.name: registration_intent
notes: registration_intent stores no secrets; new_secret MUST only be processed at sign_up_complete.
Creating a new pending registration for the same (org_id,target_identifier_hash) MUST revoke prior pending registration intents (latest-wins).

resources.description: Abuse-safe OTP challenge for consumer proof (SMS/email). Stores only destination_hash + code_hash; enforces max_attempts, lockout, expiry, and single-use consumption (status: active|consumed|locked|expired|revoked).
resources.name: consumer_otp_challenge

resources.description: Session-bound proof record produced by consumer OTP/passkey flows. Distinct from IAM-3 StepUpGrant; MUST NOT satisfy any aal2_strong requirement (status: active|expired|revoked).
resources.name: consumer_proof_grant

dependencies.reason: Policy engine contract for auth context + tiered assurance naming; required to prevent consumer OTP from being treated as strong step-up.
Tenant key semantics (org_id), membership linking, cross-tenant isolation invariants + boundary hide-existence profile.
Boundary security posture: uniform tenant-safe responses, timing hardening, and anti-enumeration requirements.
Canonical error envelope + top-level code registry for uniform responses.
Outbox/Oban queue quality controls for invite/email/token dispatch jobs.
OTP destinations (email/phone) MUST be stored via PII-1 or as irreversible hashes; IAM-2 stores destination_hash only.
Registry head parity (Phase 5). IAM-2 does not emit events but aligns to registry law for suite consistency.

uniform_response_rules: All cross-tenant and unauthorized access outcomes MUST use ERR_NOT_FOUND (hide existence) and MUST NOT expose whether a resource exists in another tenant.
All hide-existence outcomes MUST use a uniform error envelope with stable shape and MUST NOT vary subcode/detail fields based on existence, tenancy, or authorization outcomes.

All boundary endpoints participating in IAM-2 workflows (invites, magic links, token redemption, membership linking) MUST apply TEN-1/SEC-1 uniform-response and timing-hardening profiles; per-path exceptions are forbidden.

supersedes.reason: CS-0@3.0.0 and BP-0@3.0.0 alignment refactor with no intended business-semantic expansion.

notes: IAM-1 defines identity primitives, authz surfaces, and enumeration hardening policy. IAM-2 defines the workflows that MUST use those primitives safely.
Where this contract specifies 'uniform responses', the response body, status code, and timing envelope MUST NOT reveal identifier existence or cross-tenant membership.

alerts.name: iam_enumeration_suspected_spike

alerts.condition: token consume failure rate exceeds baseline per purpose
alerts.name: iam_token_consume_failure_spike

release_blocks: If enumeration_suspected alert triggers continuously for 15 minutes, deployments that touch IAM flows MUST be paused pending investigation.

never_owns: Authorization decisions (roles/capabilities, risk tagging, strong assurance policy) — IAM-1.
Strong step-up and admin MFA factors (TOTP/WebAuthn), StepUpGrant issuance, delegated admin resets — IAM-3.
Payout release, exports, DSAR privileged operations (governed via IAM-1 + BI/DSAR/LED contracts).
Storing plaintext destinations (email/phone); destinations MUST be handled via PII-1 or stored only as irreversible hashes.
owns: Registration & account bootstrap (consumers and org staff).
AAL1 authentication strategies and credential lifecycle: password, magic link, OAuth (Google/Apple).
Invite lifecycle for org onboarding (invites, acceptance, expiry).
Password reset and email verification flows.
Consumer OTP challenges (SMS/email) for low-risk consumer proof (e.g., ticket transfer, consumer account recovery steps).
Issuance of session-bound ConsumerProofGrant records (NOT StepUpGrant) used only for low-risk policy checks in IAM-1.

references.reason: Export/auth re-check pattern (GC-032) that IAM-2 workflows must enable for identity-related exports or audit artifacts.
Observability baseline for security signals and abuse detection.

consumer_otp_controls.code_storage: code_hash only (argon2id recommended) + server-side pepper; no plaintext
consumer_otp_controls.destination_storage: destination_hash only; plaintext destination in PII-1 only

enumeration_protection.recommended_behavior: Always return a success-looking response with correlation_id; mask destinations; never confirm account existence.

summary:
Defines tenant-safe identity lifecycle workflows (invites, proofs, and linking) to prevent cross-tenant user existence leaks (GC-030) and to ensure async workflow steps re-check authorization at execution time.

 Phase-5 note: IAM-2 is a non-producer contract; its internal dispatch/outbox spec is NOT the EVT bus outbox. EVT bus emission is disabled (emits_events=false, outbox_events=[]).

notes: All invite and membership-granting workflows MUST be scoped to org_id and MUST NOT disclose information about identities or memberships in other orgs.
Proof tokens MUST encode scope (purpose + org_id when applicable) and workers MUST validate that scope before applying side effects.

title: IAM-2 Identity Lifecycle Workflows and Proof Tokens

invariants: Rate limit requests per destination_hash and per request_ip_hash.
Enforce resend cooldown (recommended 30s).
Create consumer_otp_challenge with status=active and expires_at_utc (recommended 10m).
uniform_response_rules: Requests MUST return a success-looking response even if the destination is unknown or unlinked (anti-enumeration).
Response MAY include masked destination and a correlation_id; MUST NOT reveal whether a user exists.

invariants: Increment attempt_count on every verification attempt (even invalid).
If attempt_count exceeds max_attempts, set locked_until_utc and status=locked.
On success, set consumer_otp_challenge status=consumed and create consumer_proof_grant with TTL (recommended 15m).
uniform_response_rules: Verification MUST return uniform error messages for invalid/expired/unknown challenges to prevent enumeration.
On success, return consumer_proof_grant_id; grant MUST be bound to session_id.

invariants: Linking a new credential to an existing account MUST require a fresh AAL1 login.
Sensitive credential changes (email/phone rotation) SHOULD require consumer proof via consumer_proof_grant.
Credential linking MUST preserve the principal identity hub (User) and attach the new credential as a spoke.
uniform_response_rules: Linking flows MUST avoid leaking whether a given email/phone is already linked to another account; return generic conflict codes.

invariants: Verification MUST bind the email identifier to a subject_user_id and MUST be idempotent.
Verification MUST NOT leak whether the email is used by another org.
Request MUST not disclose whether the identifier exists.
Consume MUST be single-use and MUST issue a session only after proof verification (session issuance itself is owned by IAM-1).
Request MUST not disclose whether the identifier exists.
Consume MUST be single-use and MUST invalidate all prior active password_reset tokens for the same subject identifier.
sign_up MUST NOT reveal whether an account exists for the identifier (uniform timing, status, and error envelope).
sign_up MUST create or refresh a RegistrationIntent bound to normalized identifier_hash and issue an email_verify ProofToken.
sign_up_complete MUST consume a valid email_verify ProofToken and finalize account activation + session creation; replay is idempotent.
If the identifier already maps to an active user, sign_up_complete MUST NOT change existing credentials and MUST return a uniform success response.
sign_up_flow.purpose: Create a new user identity without leaking whether an account already exists for a target identifier (GC-030).

silent_link_invite_flow.goal: Allow an authorized actor to invite an identifier to join org_id without learning whether the identifier already exists on the platform or is a member of another org (GC-030).
invariants: invite_request MUST return a uniform response regardless of whether the identifier exists.
invite_accept MUST only grant membership for the invite's org_id and MUST verify the token purpose and scope.
If the subject already has an account, the flow MUST link silently (no disclosure to inviter). If not, the flow MUST allow sign-up and then link.

approved_authority_corrections.identity_resolution: All password, magic-link, OAuth, and service-token authentication resolves through a trusted provider to global AuthIdentity keyed by exact (issuer, provider_subject), before organization selection. Email equality MUST NOT merge principals. IAM-2 MUST NOT access PII-1 subject_lookup_key_hash.
